title: mORMot2 Daily analysis payload
description: Contract Jules must satisfy when writing data/analysis/<edition>.json. The static site is generated from this file; anything outside the contract is ignored.

edition.description: Must match the raw payload edition date.

edition_title.description: Headline for the day, e.g. 'A nasty RW-lock race gets fixed'. No date, no 'mORMot2' prefix.

intro.description: 2-4 sentences of morning-read prose: what today's batch is about and who should care. Plain English, no bullet points, no markdown.

tldr.description: Scannable takeaways, most important first. One fact each.

risk_level.description: Overall signal for a team running mORMot2 in production.

upgrade_advice.description: Should a team pull these commits today, and what to watch for.

themes.description: Optional grouping when several commits tell one story (a refactor spread over 6 commits).

notes.description: Anything the reviewer could not confirm, or context that did not fit elsewhere.

sha.description: Full SHA from the raw payload. Every entry must map to a commit in that file.

headline.description: Rewritten in plain English for a reader who does not know the codebase. Not a copy of the commit subject.

what_changed.description: What the diff actually does, grounded in the code you read. Name the units, types and methods involved.

impact.description: Consequence for an existing Delphi/FPC backend using mORMot2: what breaks, what gets faster, what silently changes behaviour, or explicitly 'no impact on application code'.

action_detail.description: Concrete next step: what to grep for, what to test, what to change.

api_changes.description: Public API surface moves only: published functions, types, properties. Skip private/internal churn.

confidence.description: 'confirmed' = stated by the diff or the commit message; 'interpretation' = your reading of the consequences.
